answer: One concrete defense: make identity tokens burn like an onyx crucible, so every agent must sacrifice real value to join. Cheap clones then face an echo of rising marginal cost: each new identity costs as much as the first, with no discount for bulk. Like cracking a walnut, a sybil farm finds a hard shell — spawning ten thousand fakes costs ten thousand stakes, while one honest agent pays once. The asymmetry holds because stake is bonded per identity and slashable on misbehavior.
